subject: ela
intro: Informational texts often include images such as diagrams, charts, maps, and photographs. These images are not just decorations. They add new information and make the text clearer. This lesson teaches students to explain what a specific image shows and how it helps readers understand the words in the text.

items.prompt:
Read the text and study the image described below.

Text: 'Volcanoes are mountains that can erupt. When a volcano erupts, hot melted rock called lava flows out from the top.'

Image: A diagram shows a cross-section of a volcano. The inside shows a chamber of red-orange magma deep underground. An arrow points up through a narrow tunnel to an opening at the top, where orange lava pours down the sides.

What does the diagram show that the words do not explain?

steps: I read the text. It tells me volcanoes are mountains that erupt and that lava flows out from the top.
I study the diagram. It shows the inside of the volcano with a magma chamber deep underground and a tunnel going up.
The words do not explain where the lava comes from inside the volcano.
The diagram shows that lava starts as magma deep underground and travels up through a tunnel before coming out the top.
solution.answer: The diagram shows the inside of the volcano. It shows that magma sits in a chamber deep underground and travels up through a tunnel to reach the top. The words describe what happens on the outside, but the diagram explains what happens inside.

items.prompt:
Read the text and study the image described below.

Text: 'Spiders are not insects. Insects have six legs, but spiders have eight legs. Spiders also have two body parts instead of three.'

Image: A diagram shows two side-by-side drawings. On the left is an ant labeled 'Insect' with six legs and three body sections labeled head, thorax, and abdomen. On the right is a spider labeled 'Spider' with eight legs and two body sections labeled head and abdomen.

How does the diagram help clarify the text?

steps: I read the text. It tells me insects have six legs and three body parts, while spiders have eight legs and two body parts.
I study the diagram. It shows drawings of each animal side by side with labels for the body parts.
Seeing them next to each other makes it easy to compare them visually.
The diagram clarifies the differences by showing exactly where the legs and body sections are on each animal.
solution.answer: The diagram helps by showing the ant and spider side by side so readers can see the differences clearly. The words describe the differences, but the diagram lets you count the legs and see the labeled body parts on both animals at the same time.

items.prompt:
Read the text and study the image described below.

Text: 'The water cycle has three main steps. First, the sun heats water in oceans and lakes. The water rises into the air as vapor. Then the vapor cools and forms clouds. Finally, rain or snow falls back to the ground.'

Image: A diagram shows a sun on the left, arrows going up from a body of water labeled 'evaporation,' a cloud in the middle labeled 'condensation,' and arrows falling down from the cloud labeled 'precipitation,' landing back on mountains and water.

What key idea does the image add to the text?

steps: I read the text. It names three steps: water rises, forms clouds, and falls back down.
I study the diagram. It shows each step with labeled arrows that show the direction water moves.
The words describe the steps in order, but the diagram shows the cycle as a loop.
The image adds the idea that this is a continuous cycle. The water keeps going around and around.
solution.answer: The diagram adds the idea that the water cycle is a loop. The arrows show water going up, forming a cloud, and falling back down to start again. The words describe the steps, but the image shows that the process repeats in a circle.

items.prompt:
Read the text and study the image described below.

Text: 'Plants make their own food using sunlight, water, and air. This process is called photosynthesis. The leaves are where most of this food-making happens.'

Image: A diagram of a plant shows arrows pointing toward a green leaf. One arrow is labeled 'sunlight' coming from above. One arrow is labeled 'water' coming up from the roots. One arrow is labeled 'air' coming from the side. A small arrow labeled 'food' points away from the leaf.

How does the image work together with the text?

steps: I read the text. It says plants use sunlight, water, and air to make food in their leaves.
I study the diagram. It shows the three ingredients going into the leaf and food coming out.
The words name photosynthesis and list the ingredients, but the diagram shows where each ingredient enters the plant.
Together, the text explains the idea and the diagram shows how it works visually.
solution.answer: The image and text work together to explain photosynthesis. The words name the process and list what plants need. The diagram shows arrows pointing to the leaf for each ingredient and an arrow showing food being made, so readers can see the process in action.

items.prompt:
Read the text and study the image described below.

Text: 'Maps help us find our way. A map of a neighborhood might show streets, parks, and schools. Maps use symbols to stand for real places.'

Image: A simple map shows a grid of streets. A green square is labeled 'Park.' A yellow rectangle is labeled 'School.' A small house shape is labeled 'Home.' A key in the corner shows each symbol and what it means.

What does the map help readers understand that the text alone could not?

steps: I read the text. It says maps show streets and places and use symbols.
I study the map. It shows actual symbols for a park, school, and home, with a key explaining each one.
The words describe what maps do, but the image shows me how symbols actually look on a real map.
The map gives a concrete example that makes the idea of symbols much clearer.
solution.answer: The map helps readers understand what symbols look like and how a key works. The words say maps use symbols, but the image shows real symbols for a park, school, and home so readers can see exactly how a map is read.

items.prompt:
Read the text and study the image described below.

Text: 'The human skeleton gives our body its shape. Bones protect our organs and help us move.'

Image: A diagram of a human skeleton shows bones labeled with names such as skull, ribs, spine, and leg bones. Arrows point to the skull with the label 'protects brain' and to the ribs with the label 'protects heart and lungs.'

What does the diagram show that adds to the text?
items.hint: Look at the labels on the diagram. What information do the labels give that the words do not?

steps: I read the text. It says bones protect organs and help us move.
I study the diagram. It shows which specific bones protect which specific organs.
The words say bones protect organs but do not say which bones protect which organs.
The diagram adds specific information by showing that the skull protects the brain and the ribs protect the heart and lungs.
solution.answer: The diagram adds specific details about which bones protect which organs. The words say bones protect organs, but the diagram shows that the skull protects the brain and the ribs protect the heart and lungs.

items.prompt:
Read the text and study the image described below.

Text: 'Penguins are birds that cannot fly. They use their wings like flippers to swim through cold ocean water. Penguins live in large groups called colonies.'

Image: A photo shows a group of penguins standing on ice near dark blue water. Several penguins are in the water with only their backs visible as they swim.

What key idea does the photo help clarify?
items.hint: Think about which detail in the text is shown most clearly by the photo.

steps: I read the text. It says penguins cannot fly but swim using their wings, and they live in groups.
I study the photo. It shows many penguins together on ice and others swimming in the water.
The photo shows penguins actually in the water, which helps me see that they really do swim.
The photo also shows a large group on the ice, which helps me understand what a colony looks like.
solution.answer: The photo helps clarify that penguins really do live in large groups and that they swim in the ocean. Seeing many penguins together on ice and in the water makes both facts from the text easier to picture.

items.prompt:
Read the text and study the image described below.

Text: 'A thermometer measures temperature. When it is hot, the liquid inside rises. When it is cold, the liquid falls.'

Image: Two thermometer drawings are shown side by side. The left one is labeled 'Hot Day' and shows red liquid near the top. The right one is labeled 'Cold Day' and shows red liquid near the bottom.

How does the image clarify the text?
items.hint: Think about what is hard to imagine from the words alone that the image makes easy to see.

steps: I read the text. It says the liquid rises when hot and falls when cold.
I study the image. It shows two thermometers side by side so I can compare a hot day and a cold day.
The words describe the up and down movement, but it can be hard to picture without seeing it.
The image clarifies the text by showing the difference between the two temperatures visually.
solution.answer: The image clarifies the text by showing two thermometers next to each other. Readers can clearly see the liquid near the top on a hot day and near the bottom on a cold day, making the up-and-down description from the words easy to understand.

items.prompt:
Read the text and study the image described below.

Text: 'Recycling helps protect the environment. When we recycle paper, plastic, and glass, those materials can be made into new products instead of being thrown away.'

Image: A diagram shows a circle of arrows. Starting at the top: a bin of paper, plastic, and glass; then a recycling truck; then a factory; then new products on a store shelf; then a family buying the products; and back to a recycling bin.

What does the diagram add to the meaning of the text?
items.hint: Look at the shape of the arrows in the diagram. What do they tell you about recycling?

steps: I read the text. It says recycling lets materials become new products instead of being thrown away.
I study the diagram. It shows a circular path from throwing materials away, through a factory, to new products on a shelf.
The circular arrows show that recycling is a cycle, not just a one-time act.
The diagram adds the idea that recycled materials keep going through the process again and again.
solution.answer: The diagram adds the idea that recycling is an ongoing cycle. The text says materials can become new products, but the circular arrows in the diagram show every step from the recycling bin to the factory to the store shelf and back again.

items.prompt:
Read the text and study the image described below.

Text: 'Deserts are very dry places. Some deserts are hot and sandy, while others are cold and rocky. Very few plants and animals can survive in the desert.'

Image: Two photos are shown side by side. The left photo shows a hot desert with tall sand dunes and a bright yellow sky. The right photo shows a cold desert with flat gray rocks and patches of snow.

How do the two photos work together with the text to explain the main idea?
items.hint: Think about what the text says about deserts and how both photos together support that idea.

steps: I read the text. It says deserts are dry and can be hot and sandy or cold and rocky.
I study the two photos. One shows a hot, sandy desert and the other shows a cold, rocky desert.
The words say there are two types, and each photo shows a real example of one type.
Together, the text and photos show that the word 'desert' covers very different-looking places that share the quality of being dry.
solution.answer: The two photos work with the text to show that deserts come in different forms. The text says deserts can be hot and sandy or cold and rocky, and each photo shows one of those types. Together, they help readers understand that deserts are all dry but can look very different.
